screens.prompt: In C2, write "Pass" if the score in B2 is 70 or more, otherwise "Fail".

hints.syntax: =IF(B2>=70,"Pass","Fail"): the test first, then the two values in order.
hints.func-if: Use IF so the label follows the score. A typed Pass is right for this one student and wrong for the next.
hints.require-ref: The test has to read B2, not a number you worked out yourself.
hints.value: Check the operator, then the order of the two values. Ana scored exactly 70, so 70>=70 passes and 70>70 does not.
hints.error: #NAME? means a label went in without quotes, so Excel hunted for a name called Pass.

reject.why: the cell would show pass, not the text the lesson asks for
IF is given only two arguments
the answer is typed, not computed
the test ignores the score cell
unquoted text is read as a name

docs.explain:
IF takes a test and returns one of two values. The test comes first, the value for a true result second, and the value for a false one third. Either value can be a number, text or another formula. Text needs quote marks, or Excel reads Pass as a name and returns #NAME?.

Ana's score is exactly 70, so =IF(B2>=70,"Pass","Fail") puts Pass in C2. Narrow the comparison to > and the same student fails, because 70 is not greater than 70. The two values are just as easy to reverse, and a reversed pair still fills the column with words, all of them wrong.

Leave the third argument out and a false test returns FALSE, so the cell shows a logical value where a label was expected. Type Pass without quotes and the formula stops with #NAME?.

errors.text: The third argument was left out, so a failing student shows FALSE instead of Fail.
Pass was written without quotes, so Excel looked for a name and found nothing.
With the labels the other way round, every passing student is marked Fail.

docs.atWork: A stock flag or a budget status is an IF underneath, and so is every pass or fail mark on a report.
docs.outcome: Write a decision that returns one of two values, chosen by a single test.

seo.title: IF in Excel: one test, two answers
seo.description: IF returns one value when a test is true and another when it is false. Ana scores 70, so the boundary between 70>=70 and 70>70 decides the exercise.
